title: Consistency and Standards
body:
**Consistency** means the same action produces the same result everywhere in a system, and
**standards** means following the conventions of the platform, even where a better one could be
invented.

The argument is about transfer. A user arrives having learned every other application they have
used, and that learning applies to a new one only where the new one behaves the same way. Save
is in the same place, the same shortcut works, the destructive action is on the right and
confirms first. Every departure costs every user the relearning, and the improvement has to be
large enough to pay for it, which it rarely is.

```
internal consistency    the same control means the same thing on every screen
external consistency    the application matches the platform's conventions
```

Internal inconsistency is the more damaging of the two, since it teaches the user a rule and
then breaks it, and a rule broken once is no longer trusted anywhere.

The tension worth naming is that consistency preserves bad conventions along with good ones. A
platform standard that predates the current hardware is still the standard, and the correct
response is usually to follow it while the alternative is not clearly better, which is a
conservative rule that [[Nielsen's Heuristics]] states directly.
